content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Tomato (*Solanum lycopersicum*) — identifiable by the compound, serrated leaflets
- **Affected part**: Leaves (multiple leaflets)
- **Lesion characteristics**:
  - Multiple discrete, circular to oval spots scattered across several leaflets
  - Dark brown to black lesion centers
  - Lighter tan/grayish margins surrounding the darker cores
  - Some lesions visible along the midrib/stem tissue
  - Background leaf tissue remains relatively green
  - Lesions of moderate size (not tiny pinpoints, not large irregular blotches)

**Differential Reasoning:**

| Disease | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Early Blight** | Strong — dark concentric lesions on tomato leaves with target-board pattern; moderate-sized discrete spots |
| Septoria Leaf Blotch | Possible but typical Septoria spots are smaller, more numerous, with pale white/gray centers and distinct dark margins (pycnidia visible) |
| Late Blight | No — Late Blight shows large, irregular water-soaked lesions with white sporulation on undersides |
| Bacterial Speck | No — Bacterial speck produces tiny specks with pronounced yellow halos |
| Leaf Mold | No — Leaf mold shows yellow patches on top surface with olive-green/brown sporulation beneath |

**Conclusion**: The lesions show the hallmark features of **Early Blight** (*Alternaria solani*): discrete, circular-to-angular dark brown lesions with concentric ring (target-board) patterning on tomato leaflets. The moderate lesion size and dark center coloration are consistent with this fungal disease.
